defs: a sudden, sharp pull or movement
a quick pull that makes something move suddenly
a short, strong tug that surprises you
exs: The bus stopped with a jerk and everyone leaned forward.
He felt a jerk on the fishing line.
With one jerk, Dad pulled the stuck door open.

defs: not tight or firmly fixed in place
able to wiggle because it is not held firmly
not held in firmly, like a wobbly tooth
exs: My front tooth is loose and wiggles when I touch it.
The loose rope slipped off the post.
A loose button fell off Carlos's coat.

defs: to throw the ball to the batter in baseball
to throw a ball toward the person who will hit it
in baseball, to send the ball to the batter
exs: Carlos will pitch the ball to his friend in the game.
It is my turn to pitch in the baseball game.
She can pitch the ball very fast and straight.

defs: to keep something in your mind and not forget it
to bring back something from the past in your mind
to think of something you learned or did before
exs: Please remember to bring your lunch box tomorrow.
I remember my first day at school.
Do you remember where we put the map?

defs: food made of fillings placed between two slices of bread
a lunch food with bread on the top and bottom
bread slices with cheese or meat in the middle
exs: Mom packed cheese sandwiches for our picnic.
We ate sandwiches by the lake at lunchtime.
Carlos made two sandwiches for himself and Mosh.

defs: shook a little because of fear or cold
shivered and could not keep still
shook in a small way, like when you feel scared
exs: Mosh trembled when the thunder boomed outside.
His hands trembled in the cold wind.
The little bird trembled on the branch.

defs: feeling that something bad might happen
feeling nervous and unhappy about a problem
thinking too much about something that may go wrong
exs: Mom was worried when Carlos came home late.
I felt worried about the big test.
Carlos looked worried when Mosh did not come back.

defs: a small number of things, usually two or so
not many, just a few
some, but only a small amount
exs: I need a couple of pencils for class.
Carlos waited for a couple of minutes at the door.
She bought a couple of apples at the store.

defs: by mistake, without meaning to
not on purpose
in a way you did not plan
exs: Carlos accidentally dropped his cup on the floor.
I accidentally stepped on my friend's toy.
Mosh accidentally knocked over the plant with his tail.

defs: to not like something at all
to feel that something is very unpleasant
to dislike something very much
exs: I hate waking up when it is still dark.
Mosh seems to hate taking a bath.
Some kids hate eating cold soup.

defs: began to shine brightly, or showed great joy
became bright, like a lamp when you switch it on
showed happiness, like a face that glows
exs: Her face lit up when she saw the birthday cake.
The room lit up when Dad turned on the lamp.
The sky lit up with colorful fireworks.

defs: a tool with a flat end used for digging
a tool for moving dirt or snow
a tool with a long handle for digging holes
exs: Carlos dug a hole in the garden with a shovel.
Dad used a shovel to clear the snow.
She brought a small shovel to the sandy beach.

defs: in a way that shows you feel a little bashful
in a quiet way, because you feel nervous around others
with a bashful smile, not wanting to speak loudly
exs: The new girl shyly said hello to the class.
He shyly held out a flower for his teacher.
Carlos shyly waved at the kids across the room.

defs: to feel nervous that something bad may happen
to think about problems and feel uneasy
to be anxious about something
exs: Don't worry, I will help you find your hat.
Mom said not to worry about the little mistake.
I worry when Mosh runs near the road.

defs: said sorry for doing something wrong
told someone that you feel bad about a mistake
said you were sorry after hurting someone's feelings
exs: Carlos apologized for breaking his sister's toy.
She apologized to the teacher for being late.
Mosh looked sad, as if he apologized with his eyes.

defs: to move slowly on your hands and knees
to move along the ground with the body low
to move like a baby or a small bug
exs: The baby likes to crawl across the living room floor.
We had to crawl under the low table.
A snail can only crawl very slowly.

defs: took in a quick breath because of surprise
breathed in suddenly because of shock
made a sharp sound with the mouth when startled
exs: Everyone gasped when the magician made the rabbit appear.
Carlos gasped when he saw the huge cake.
She gasped as the door suddenly opened.

defs: to complain in a low, unhappy voice
to say unhappy things quietly because you are annoyed
to mutter about something you do not like
exs: My brother likes to grumble when it is time to clean up.
Dad began to grumble about the long line.
Do not grumble, just try the new food.

defs: to say you will give or do something for someone
to hold something out for someone to take
to ask if someone would like some help or a gift
exs: I will offer Mosh a treat if he sits.
Carlos wanted to offer his seat to the old man.
They offer free juice at the school party.

defs: many things put one on top of another
a heap of things lying together
a big stack of things in one place
exs: There was a big pile of leaves in the yard.
Carlos left a pile of books on his desk.
A pile of snow fell off the roof.

defs: held out a finger to show something
showed where something was with a finger
stretched out an arm to show a direction
exs: Carlos pointed at the bird in the tree.
The teacher pointed to the board.
Mosh pointed his nose toward the food.

defs: completely spoiled and not good any more
damaged so badly that it cannot be used
spoiled, like a toy that is totally broken
exs: The rain ruined our picnic lunch.
My drawing was ruined when I spilled juice on it.
The muddy puppy ruined the clean floor.

defs: a big bag or case for carrying clothes on a trip
a case you pack when you go on vacation
a box with a handle for travel things
exs: Mom packed a suitcase for our trip to the beach.
Carlos pulled his heavy suitcase down the hall.
Her suitcase was full of warm clothes.

defs: the worst of all
less good than every other one
the one that is the worst of all
exs: That was the worst storm we ever had.
Spinach is the worst food in the world, said Carlos.
It was the worst day of the whole trip.

defs: a very high sound, like a tiny bird or mouse
a sound that is thin, sharp and high
a voice or sound that goes up high
exs: The little mouse made a high-pitched squeak.
Her high-pitched laugh made everyone smile.
The kettle gave a high-pitched sound.

defs: making a musical sound by blowing air through your lips
making a thin, airy sound like wind
blowing out air to make a tune
exs: Dad was whistling a happy song in the kitchen.
The wind was whistling through the trees.
Carlos walked home whistling a tune.

defs: in a way that shows you can't wait
in a very happy and eager way
with great joy and lots of energy
exs: Carlos excitedly opened the big box.
The kids excitedly ran to the lake.
Mosh excitedly jumped up and down at the door.

defs: swapped seats so each had the other's spot
moved into each other's spot
changed spots with each other
exs: Carlos and Dad traded places so Carlos could steer the boat.
The two kids traded places on the swing.
We traded places in line so my friend could stand with me.

defs: a wooden platform built out over the water
a place where boats stop and people step on or off
a flat walkway beside a lake for boats
exs: We sat on the dock and watched the fish.
The boat was tied to the dock.
Carlos jumped off the dock into the cool lake.

defs: small radios that let people talk from far away
hand-held radios used to speak to a friend nearby
small devices for sending voices over a short distance
exs: Carlos and his friend used walkie-talkies to talk across the field.
The campers had walkie-talkies in their bags.
Mosh barked when the walkie-talkies made a loud noise.

defs: extremely dirty
covered in mud and dirt
very unclean and in need of a wash
exs: Carlos's shoes were filthy after the muddy game.
The filthy old rag smelled bad.
Mosh came home filthy from playing in the mud.

defs: to think the same way as someone else
to say yes to a plan or idea
to have the same opinion as another person
exs: I agree that pizza is the best lunch.
Carlos and his sister agree to share the toy.
Do you agree with my plan to build a fort?

defs: a machine that sucks up dust from the floor
a cleaning machine that pulls dirt into a bag
a household machine used to clean carpets
exs: Mom used the vacuum to clean the rug.
The robot vacuum rolled across the kitchen floor.
Mosh is afraid of the loud vacuum.

defs: making loud, hard, banging sounds
making a noisy sound like metal pieces hitting
rattling noisily, like pots hitting each other
exs: We heard the clattering of pots in the kitchen.
The robot walked down the hall, clattering all the way.
A clattering sound came from the toolbox.

defs: a small metal piece with a spiral that you turn to join things
a small pointed metal piece twisted in with a tool
a tiny metal piece that holds parts together
exs: Dad used a tool to turn the screw into the wood.
One screw fell out of the robot's arm.
Carlos looked for the missing screw on the floor.

defs: the soil on the ground
the brown stuff that plants grow in
loose earth that can make things messy
exs: Mosh dug in the dirt and made a big hole.
Carlos had dirt on his hands after gardening.
The truck's wheels threw up dirt on the road.

defs: to spring up and down again and again
to jump back after hitting something hard
to hop up after hitting the ground, like a ball
exs: The rubber ball will bounce high on the floor.
Mosh loves to bounce around the yard.
The kids bounce on the trampoline after school.

defs: things that were done wrong
errors that you make when you do something
wrong answers or wrong actions
exs: Everyone makes mistakes when they learn something new.
Carlos fixed the mistakes in his spelling test.
The teacher circled two mistakes on my page.

defs: saw something suddenly or noticed it
noticed something that was hard to see
found something by looking carefully
exs: Carlos spotted a bird's nest in the tree.
I spotted my friend in the big crowd.
Mosh spotted a squirrel near the fence.

defs: a list at the front of a book showing its parts
a page that tells you where each story begins
a list of chapters with page numbers
exs: Look at the table of contents to find the chapter.
The table of contents shows that story three starts on page ten.
Carlos read the table of contents before opening the book.

defs: in the direction of something
moving closer to someone or something
heading to a place or person
exs: Mosh ran toward the door when he heard Carlos.
The ship sailed toward the shore.
She walked toward her friends at the park.

defs: a thin line where something has started to break
a narrow gap in a wall or glass
a small split in something hard
exs: There was a crack in the old cup.
Carlos saw light through a crack in the door.
A crack ran across the ice on the pond.

defs: a building or room where a car is kept
a place at home for parking cars and storing tools
a room beside a house for a car and bikes
exs: Dad parked the car in the garage.
Carlos found his old bike in the garage.
The tools are kept on a shelf in the garage.

defs: to laugh in a soft, high way
to laugh quietly because something is funny
to make little laughing sounds
exs: The baby began to giggle when Carlos made a face.
I could not stop giggling in class.
Mosh made the girls giggle with his funny dance.

defs: to look quickly and secretly at something
to take a quick look, often through a small space
to look at something that you are not supposed to see yet
exs: Carlos tried to peek at his birthday gift.
She opened the door a little to peek outside.
Mosh likes to peek through the fence.

defs: without making much sound
in a calm way without noise
in a soft way so others can sleep
exs: The class sat quietly while the teacher read.
Carlos walked quietly past the sleeping baby.
Mosh crept quietly across the floor.

defs: lifted both shoulders to show you do not know
raised the shoulders to say I don't care
moved shoulders up and down to answer without words
exs: When asked why, Carlos shrugged and said nothing.
She shrugged because she did not know the answer.
Dad shrugged and smiled at the funny question.

defs: a time when you are able to do something
a moment that lets you try something
an opening to do something you want
exs: Everyone will get a chance to ride the pony.
Carlos had a chance to win the race.
Give the new boy a chance to play.

defs: to close something so that it stays in place
to join or close, like a belt or buckle
to do up buttons or a seat belt
exs: Please fasten your seat belt in the car.
Carlos could not fasten his coat because his hands were cold.
She had to fasten the lid tightly.

defs: to turn from solid to liquid because of heat
to change into water when it gets warm
to become soft and wet when warm, like ice
exs: The snowman will melt when the sun comes out.
Ice cream starts to melt on a hot day.
Mosh watched the ice melt in his bowl.

defs: to lift up food with a spoon or a flat tool
to take something out with a curved tool
to pick up a soft thing with a spoon
exs: Carlos used a spoon to scoop the ice cream.
Please scoop some rice into my bowl.
Dad will scoop the sand into a bucket.

defs: to slide by accident and lose your balance
to slide on a wet or icy place and fall
to move away smoothly by mistake
exs: Be careful not to slip on the icy path.
Carlos began to slip on the wet floor.
My sock made me slip on the smooth floor.

defs: a big storm with lots of snow and strong wind
very bad winter weather with heavy snow
weather where snow falls hard and wind blows
exs: School was closed because of the snowstorm.
We stayed home during the snowstorm and drank hot cocoa.
Mosh did not like the cold wind of the snowstorm.

defs: A small set of steps leading up to a door
The little porch at the front of a house
Steps outside a building where you can sit
exs: Carlos sat on the stoop and waited for his friend.
Snow covered the stoop, so Dad swept it clean.
The cat slept on the stoop in the warm sun.

defs: The grip that stops your shoes or tires from slipping
Grip between a surface and something moving on it
What boots need on ice so you do not slide
exs: Boots with rough bottoms give you good traction on ice.
The car tires had no traction on the icy road.
Mosh's paws had little traction on the slippery floor.

defs: To cut shapes out of wood, ice, or snow
To make a statue by cutting away pieces
To slowly cut a design into something hard
exs: Grandpa likes to carve little birds from wood.
We will carve a big pumpkin face for Halloween.
They carve a dragon out of a block of ice.

defs: A game where people try to win a prize
An event where people try to be the best
A race or game with a winner at the end
exs: Carlos entered the snow contest at school.
She won first prize in the spelling contest.
The pie contest has ten bakers this year.

defs: Deciding who did best in a game or show
Looking at things carefully to pick the winner
Deciding who wins after seeing people's work
exs: The mayor is judging the snow sculptures today.
Judging starts at noon, so please be ready.
Mom was judging the cake table with a smile.

defs: The leader of a town or city
The person chosen to run a city
Someone who is in charge of a town
exs: The mayor gave a speech in the town square.
Our mayor cut the ribbon to open the park.
Carlos shook hands with the mayor at the fair.

defs: A small copy of a real thing
A toy-sized version of something bigger
A smaller copy built to show how something looks
exs: Carlos built a model of a rocket.
She made a model of the school from paper.
Dad has a model of an old ship on his shelf.

defs: To stretch out your arm to touch something
To arrive at a place after traveling
To be tall enough to touch something high
exs: Carlos cannot reach the top shelf without a stool.
We will reach the camp before dark.
Mosh jumped but could not reach the ball.

defs: A long thin strip of cloth used for tying or decoration
A pretty band you can tie in a bow
A strip of cloth given as a prize
exs: She tied a red ribbon in her hair.
The winner got a blue ribbon.
Dad wrapped the gift with a shiny ribbon.

defs: A work of art made from stone, ice, or clay
An art piece you can walk around and see from all sides
A statue shaped from snow or metal
exs: The snow sculpture looked like a giant bear.
We saw a metal sculpture in the park.
Her clay sculpture of a dog sat on the desk.

defs: A robot that is made of snow
A snow figure that can move like a machine
A frosty robot friend built by kids in winter
exs: The snowbot waved its stick arms at Carlos.
Our snowbot rolled across the yard on its own.
Carlos gave the snowbot a carrot nose.

defs: To think something is probably true
To guess or imagine that something is so
To believe something will happen without being sure
exs: I suppose it will snow tonight.
Do you suppose Mosh is hungry again?
I suppose we can go home now.

defs: A sport played with rackets and a small ball over a net
A game where two players hit a ball back and forth
A sport played on a court with a net in the middle
exs: Carlos plays tennis with his sister on Saturdays.
The tennis ball bounced over the fence.
She hit the tennis ball over the net.

defs: A small hill or lump on a path
A sudden hit or knock against something
A raised round spot on a surface
exs: The sled hit a bump and flew up.
I have a bump on my head from the fall.
Dad felt a bump as the car went over the road.

defs: Pulling something heavy along the ground
Pulling something slowly behind you
Moving a thing by tugging it across the floor
exs: Carlos was dragging his sled up the hill.
She was dragging a heavy bag across the yard.
Mosh came in dragging his blanket behind him.

defs: To bend your body to one side
To rest against something for support
To tilt your body forward or sideways
exs: Lean to the left to turn the sled.
Carlos likes to lean on the fence and watch.
Please do not lean out of the window.

defs: A very short amount of time
A tiny part of time, like a second or two
A short wait
exs: Wait a moment while I tie my shoes.
For one moment, everything was quiet.
At that moment, the school bell rang.

defs: A person riding in a vehicle who is not driving
Someone who travels on a bus, train, or plane
A rider who sits in a car but does not steer
exs: Carlos was the passenger on his sister's sled.
Every passenger on the bus had a seat.
The passenger put her bag under the seat.

defs: A person who rides a sled down a hill
Someone who slides down snowy slopes for fun
A kid who zooms over snow on a board with runners
exs: The little sledder laughed all the way down.
Each sledder waited for a turn at the top.
A fast sledder zoomed past Carlos.

defs: A big pile of snow blown by the wind
A deep heap of snow piled up in one place
A mound of snow against a wall or fence
exs: The sled crashed into a soft snowdrift.
Wind made a tall snowdrift by the door.
Mosh jumped into the snowdrift and disappeared.

defs: Not common or normal
Strange because it is not seen often
Different from what you expect
exs: A purple dog is an unusual sight.
It was unusual to see snow in October.
She wore an unusual hat with feathers.

defs: A big wild animal
A large, scary-looking animal in a story
An animal, especially a big strong one
exs: In the dream, a hairy beast chased Carlos.
The beast in the story had green eyes.
Mosh looked like a funny little beast in his costume.

defs: A big hole inside a mountain or hillside
A dark space in the rock where bats may live
A natural room under the ground
exs: The bear slept in a cave all winter.
We shone a flashlight into the cave.
Bats hung from the roof of the cave.

defs: To bend down quickly to avoid something
To lower your head fast so you do not get hit
To crouch down in a hurry
exs: Duck down quickly! A snowball is coming right at us!
Carlos had to duck to get under the low branch.
Tall Dad must duck when he enters the tent.

defs: Got free from a place or from danger
Ran away and got out safely
Got away from something that held you
exs: The hamster escaped from its cage.
Carlos escaped from the beast in his dream.
We escaped the rain by running inside.

defs: A large area covered with many trees
A big wild place full of trees
A place where many trees grow close together
exs: We walked through the forest to find the camp.
Deer live in the forest near our town.
Birds sang in the green forest.

defs: Weighing a lot and hard to lift
Not light, so it is difficult to carry
Having great weight
exs: The backpack was too heavy for Carlos.
Dad lifted the heavy box with both hands.
The heavy rock sank in the pond.

defs: Resting flat on a bed or the ground
Being in a flat position, not standing or sitting
Staying flat on your back or stomach
exs: Mosh was lying on the rug.
Carlos was lying in bed when he heard a noise.
We were lying on the grass looking at clouds.

defs: Was able to do something difficult
Succeeded in doing something after trying hard
Found a way to get something done
exs: Carlos managed to climb over the log.
She managed to carry all four bags.
We managed to finish before the bell.
